intro.data: One pipeline must process TWO batches: a small batch (2) and a large batch (5). Bring in both stepping-stone tables (Normalized, Scaled) and chain three machines — Increment (+1), Double (x2), Finalize (+4) — to turn each batch into its true report. The tray hides look-alikes at every stage, and one sneaky machine 'Bump' matches Double on the small batch but drifts on the large one. A pipeline that only gets the small batch right is still wrong; build the chain that nails BOTH.
intro.alchemy: One process must refine TWO charges: a light charge (2) and a heavy charge (5). Bring in both stepping-stone vessels (Tempered, Concentrated) and chain three apparatuses — Quicken (+1), Redouble (x2), Seal (+4) — to turn each charge into its true alloy. The tray hides look-alikes at every stage, and a sly 'Nudge' matches Redouble on the light charge but drifts on the heavy one. A process that only gets the light charge right is still false; build the chain that nails BOTH.
intro.spellcraft: One rite must bind TWO sparks: a faint spark (2) and a fierce spark (5). Bring in both stepping-stone flames (Steadied, Swelled) and chain three runes — Quicken (+1), Redouble (x2), Seal (+4) — to turn each spark into its true ward. The tray hides look-alikes at every stage, and a sly 'Nudge' matches Redouble on the faint spark but drifts on the fierce one. A rite that only binds the faint spark is still hollow; build the chain that nails BOTH.
intro.abstract: Here numbers are the carried values and a prime b′ is a different value of the same type. One pipeline A→B→C→D must satisfy two cases over the same start A and goal D: case 1 sends 2 ↦ 10, case 2 sends 5 ↦ 16. Compose f (+1), g (×2), h (+4); each stage has a same-typed impostor, and g? (+3) coincides with g at one value so it passes case 1 but fails case 2. Build the one chain that passes both and leave the impostors in the tray.

goal.data: Bring both stepping-stone tables and the three faithful machines, and wire ONE pipeline that turns batch 2 into report 10 AND batch 5 into report 16.
goal.alchemy: Bring both stepping-stone vessels and the three faithful apparatuses, and wire ONE process that turns charge 2 into alloy 10 AND charge 5 into alloy 16.
goal.spellcraft: Bring both stepping-stone flames and the three faithful runes, and wire ONE rite that turns spark 2 into ward 10 AND spark 5 into ward 16.
goal.abstract: Place B and C and the faithful machines, and wire one A→D chain that sends 2 ↦ 10 and 5 ↦ 16.

afterSuccess.data: One pipeline handled both batches: Increment, Double, Finalize sent 2 to 10 and 5 to 16. The 'Bump' machine doubled-by-coincidence on the small batch but added 3 on the large one, so it passed the easy case and failed the hard one. That second batch is why a pipeline is the composite of correct steps, not steps that merely happen to agree once: report = h ∘ g ∘ f.
afterSuccess.alchemy: One process handled both charges: Quicken, Redouble, Seal sent 2 to 10 and 5 to 16. 'Nudge' matched Redouble on the light charge by coincidence but drifted on the heavy one, passing the easy case and failing the hard one. The second charge is why a process is the composite of correct steps: h ∘ g ∘ f.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: One rite bound both sparks: Quicken, Redouble, Seal sent 2 to 10 and 5 to 16. 'Nudge' matched Redouble on the faint spark by coincidence but drifted on the fierce one, passing the easy case and failing the hard one. The second spark is why a rite is the composite of correct steps: h ∘ g ∘ f.
afterSuccess.abstract: The faithful composite h ∘ g ∘ f sent 2 ↦ 10 and 5 ↦ 16. g? = +3 coincides with g = ×2 at 3 (both give 6), so it passes case 1, but at 6 it gives 9 not 12 and fails case 2. Two cases pin the behavior: agreeing on one input is not equality of morphisms.

reveal.summary: Two test cases over one pipeline force every stage to be genuinely correct, not coincidentally right on a single input. h ∘ g ∘ f : A → D must send 2 ↦ 10 AND 5 ↦ 16; an impostor that matches a faithful step at just one value still corrupts the composite on another.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: const pipeline = (x: number) => x + 1 |> double |> (+4); a unit test on one input can pass a buggy stage — a second case catches it.
